lead: Rejudge or rescore many submissions by a filter: one problem, one contest, one user, one judge or the whole site.

filter.title: Submission filter
filter.idHint: Submission ids follow the submission time. The date range above is usually enough.
filter.forceHint: By default submissions past their lock time are skipped.
filter.lockedNote: Submissions still held by a judge and the final-judging submissions of a contest are always skipped.
filter.contestHint: Only this contest's submissions (its editors may run it).
filter.judgedOnHint: Only submissions this judge graded last.
filter.siteWide: No problem or contest: the action covers the whole site and needs judge.edit_all_problem.

summary.title: Selected filter
summary.countNote: The number of matching submissions shows in the confirm: pressing “Rejudge” counts first and resets nothing.

done: Queued {count} submissions for rejudging. They run at batch priority and emit no per-submission events, so the submission table updates when a judge picks them up.

confirm.title: Rejudge the matching submissions?
confirm.body: The submissions that match are reset to waiting: their current result and points are cleared until judging ends. This cannot be undone.

count.countingText: Asking the server (dryRun). Nothing has been reset.
count.needsLot: submissions match, over the limit of {limit}. Needs judge.rejudge_submission_lot; narrow the filter or ask someone who holds it.

errors.dateOrder: The end must be after the start.

rescore.title: Recalculate points of the matching submissions?
rescore.preview: {count} graded submissions match; {problems} problems and {contests} contests will be recalculated.
rescore.body: Points are recomputed from each test's result with the problem's current points and partial setting, then user points and contest results follow. Use it after changing a problem's points.
rescore.done: Queued recalculation of {problems} problems and {contests} contests ({count} matching submissions).

progress.waiting: {count} submissions still waiting for a judge.
